name: The Philadelphia Inquirer editorial board
lean_basis: Largest newspaper in Pennsylvania. The editorial board still endorses; it backed Josh Shapiro for governor on Oct. 9, 2022 and Kamala Harris in 2024. AllSides rates Inquirer news coverage Lean Left. The board is separate from the newsroom.

name: Pittsburgh Post-Gazette
lean_basis: Since May 4, 2026 the Post-Gazette has been published by the Venetoulis Institute for Local Journalism, the 501(c)(3) nonprofit that also owns The Baltimore Banner (post-gazette.com/about). Federal tax law bars 501(c)(3) groups from endorsing candidates, and its site has no opinion section, so it is not endorsing in 2026. The Block-era board's past picks (Trump 2020, Oz 2022) no longer apply. AllSides rates its news Center (Jan. 2022 review, low confidence).

name: Pittsburgh Tribune-Review (TribLive) editorial board
lean_basis: Ad Fontes rates TribLive Middle (-1.04). Founded by Richard Mellon Scaife, its opinion page has a conservative history. Earlier research found it stopped endorsing candidates in 2016; that was not re-confirmed in this pass. Included so Pittsburgh readers know not to look for a pick.

name: League of Women Voters of Pennsylvania (VOTE411)
lean_basis: Nonpartisan. Never endorses or opposes candidates. Takes positions only on ballot measures. Publishes candidate questionnaire answers on VOTE411.org.

name: Pennsylvania AFL-CIO
lean_basis: State federation of unions, about 700,000 members. Endorses through its political committee; endorses Democrats in nearly every statewide race.

name: Pennsylvania State Education Association (PSEA-PACE)
lean_basis: Largest teachers' union in the state (about 178,000 members). Its PAC, PSEA-PACE, mostly endorses Democrats, with some Republican legislators.

name: National Federation of Independent Business, Pennsylvania (NFIB PA PAC)
lean_basis: Small-business lobby. Its PAC endorses on tax and regulation records and backs Republicans in most statewide races. Used here in place of the Pennsylvania Chamber, whose PAC had not announced a 2026 governor pick as of Oct. 13.

name: Conservation Voters of Pennsylvania
lean_basis: State affiliate of the League of Conservation Voters. Endorses mostly Democrats; backed Shapiro in April 2022.

name: Planned Parenthood Pennsylvania PAC
lean_basis: Abortion-rights political arm of Planned Parenthood in Pennsylvania. Endorses candidates who support abortion access.

name: Pennsylvania Pro-Life Federation (LifePAC)
lean_basis: State affiliate of National Right to Life. Its LifePAC endorses anti-abortion candidates, nearly all Republicans.

name: Giffords PAC
lean_basis: Gun-safety group founded by former Rep. Gabby Giffords. Endorses candidates who support stricter firearms laws. Included as the gun-policy counterweight; the NRA Political Victory Fund had not posted a 2026 Pennsylvania governor grade or endorsement as of Oct. 16.

name: NRA Political Victory Fund
lean_basis: Gun-rights PAC. Grades and endorses candidates by their positions on firearms laws; endorsements go almost entirely to Republicans.

name: Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 5 (Philadelphia police union)
lean_basis: Philadelphia's police union, about 14,000 active and retired members. Has endorsed Republicans for president (Trump in 2016, 2020, 2024) and candidates of both parties in state and local races. The Pennsylvania State Lodge FOP had no 2026 governor endorsement found; Lodge 5 is listed because it is the largest police union in the two places this guide serves.

name: Pennsylvania State Troopers Association
lean_basis: Union for state police troopers, about 4,000 active members. Endorses in statewide races based on public-safety and pension records; has backed candidates of both parties (Tom Corbett in 2010, Josh Shapiro in 2022 and 2026).
